title: Treatment of Goodwill in Partnership Accounts
outcomes: Explain the meaning of goodwill, the factors that affect it and when it needs to be valued.
Apply the accounting standard rule that inherent goodwill is not recognised and adjust goodwill through capital accounts instead.
Value goodwill by the average profit (simple and weighted), super profit (years' purchase, annuity, capitalisation) and capitalisation of average profit methods.
Compute sacrificing and gaining ratios and pass goodwill entries on admission, change in ratio, retirement and death.

meta.exam_tip: Goodwill appears inside almost every admission, retirement and death question. Get the sacrifice/gain table right first — the entries follow automatically.

concepts.title: What goodwill is and what creates it
body: Goodwill is the value of a firm's reputation that lets it expect future profits above the normal profits earned by similar businesses. In plain words, it is the likelihood that existing customers keep coming back.

It is an intangible asset — it cannot be seen or touched — but it is real: a buyer will pay more than the net assets for a business that earns super profits. If net assets are worth ₹5 lakh and a buyer pays ₹6 lakh, ₹1 lakh is paid for goodwill.

Factors that build goodwill: quality of goods or service; personal reputation and skill of the owners; location (e.g. a busy market); near-monopoly rights such as a sole dealership; trademarks and patents; managerial ability; research that lowers cost or improves quality; favourable long-term contracts for materials.
Goodwill needs valuing when the profit-sharing ratio changes, a partner is admitted, a partner retires or dies, and when the business is dissolved or sold.
concepts.analogy: Two tea stalls sell the same tea at the same price, but one always has a queue. The queue is goodwill — and anyone buying that stall would pay extra for it.
concepts.work: Valuation of goodwill is a negotiation point in every change of partners; CAs often prepare the valuation note that partners sign.

concepts.title: Accounting standard view: no self-generated goodwill in the books
body: Under AS 26 (Intangible Assets), an intangible can be recognised only if it is identifiable, the enterprise controls its future economic benefits, and its cost can be measured reliably. Internally generated (inherent) goodwill fails these tests — it is not separable, its benefits are uncertain and no cost was paid for it — so it is not recognised.
Only purchased goodwill — goodwill for which money or money's worth was actually paid (e.g. paying ₹3 lakh for net assets of ₹2.5 lakh) — may be recorded.
Therefore, on admission, retirement, death or a change in ratio, Goodwill Account is NOT raised in the books. The agreed value is used only to compensate partners through their capital accounts.
If a Goodwill Account already exists in the books at the time of reconstitution, it is written off immediately among the old partners in their old ratio, whether it was purchased or not.
concepts.analogy: You can't put "I am popular" on your balance sheet; you can only show the price you actually paid when you bought someone else's popular shop.
concepts.work: Auditors object when a firm raises goodwill on reconstitution just to inflate capital balances — it overstates assets and misleads banks.

concepts.title: Average profit method — simple and weighted
body: Goodwill = average profit × number of years' purchase. Past profits are first adjusted for abnormal or non-recurring items (fire loss, one-off gains), for expected future changes (e.g. a fair salary to working partners, loss of a contract) and for income from non-trade investments.
Simple average: total adjusted profits ÷ number of years — used when profits show no clear trend.
Weighted average: profits multiplied by weights (usually 1, 2, 3 … with the highest weight on the latest year), total ÷ sum of weights — used when profits clearly rise or fall.
The number of years' purchase is a matter of judgement and negotiation — it represents how many years the advantage is expected to last.
concepts.analogy: Judging a batsman: if his scores are steadily improving, you trust his recent innings more (weighted); if they bounce around, you take his plain average.
concepts.work: In practice the adjustment of past profits is where most negotiation happens — e.g. whether a one-time government subsidy should be removed.

concepts.title: Super profit methods
body: Super profit = average maintainable profit − normal profit, where normal profit = capital employed × normal rate of return (NRR) of similar firms.

Steps: (1) find capital employed (assets − outside liabilities, excluding goodwill, fictitious assets and non-trade investments); (2) find the average maintainable profit; (3) apply the NRR to capital employed; (4) subtract. No super profit, no goodwill.
(a) Number of years' purchase: goodwill = super profit × years.

(b) Annuity method: goodwill = super profit × present value of an annuity of ₹1 for the given years at the given rate — it recognises the time value of money, so it gives a lower figure than multiplying the super profit by the same number of years.
(c) Capitalisation of super profit: goodwill = super profit ÷ NRR (× 100 when NRR is in %).
Logic: an incoming partner pays only for the excess earnings, because normal profit could be earned by investing the same capital in any similar business.
concepts.analogy: If any shop in the market earns ₹1 lakh on ₹10 lakh, and yours earns ₹1.4 lakh, the extra ₹40,000 a year is what a buyer pays for.
concepts.work: Valuers use super-profit logic for professional practices (CA, medical, legal firms) where the partners' personal skill drives excess earnings.

concepts.title: Capitalisation of average profit
body: Normal value of the business = average profit ÷ NRR. Goodwill = normal value − actual capital employed (net assets).
If the same average profit and capital employed are used, this gives exactly the same figure as capitalising the super profit, because (P ÷ r) − C = (P − r × C) ÷ r.
concepts.analogy: Ask: "What would I have to invest elsewhere at the normal rate to earn this profit?" Whatever exceeds the assets actually invested is goodwill.
concepts.work: This is the crude ancestor of the earnings-capitalisation methods analysts use to value businesses.

concepts.title: Why goodwill is valued when partners change
body: Every reconstitution changes future shares: some partners give up part of their share (sacrifice), others get more (gain). The gainers should compensate the sacrificers for the value they give up.
Sacrifice = old share − new share (positive). Gain = new share − old share (positive). Compensation = goodwill of the firm × fraction sacrificed or gained.
concepts.analogy: If you hand over a slice of your pizza to a newcomer, it is fair that the newcomer pays you for that slice — and goodwill decides the price of the whole pizza.
concepts.work: Disputes on reconstitution are mostly about the sacrifice/gain calculation; a clean ratio table attached to the deed prevents them.

concepts.title: Goodwill on admission of a new partner
body: Sacrificing ratio = old share − new share for each old partner. If only the newcomer's share is given (and nothing about who gives it up), the old partners sacrifice in their old ratio.

Case 1 — premium brought in cash: Bank A/c Dr (capital + premium), To New Partner's Capital A/c (capital), To Old Partners' Capital A/cs (premium, in the sacrificing ratio). Only partners who sacrifice get a share.
Case 2 — no cash for goodwill: New Partner's Capital A/c Dr, To Old Partners' Capital A/cs (his share of goodwill, sacrificing ratio). Partly in cash: combine both entries.
Case 3 — premium paid privately to the old partners: no entry in the firm's books (the amount each receives should still follow the sacrificing ratio).
Existing goodwill in the books is first written off to the old partners in their old ratio.
concepts.analogy: The newcomer buys a ticket to join the profits. If he pays at the counter (cash), the money is passed to the sellers; if he can't pay now, the ticket price is entered against his own account.
concepts.work: When a new partner joins a CA firm, the admission agreement states the goodwill value and whether it is paid in cash or adjusted — the accountant passes exactly these entries.

concepts.title: Goodwill on change in ratio, retirement and death
body: Change in profit-sharing ratio (no one joins or leaves): value goodwill; gainers' capital accounts are debited and sacrificers' credited with goodwill × fraction gained/sacrificed. A partner with no change is left out.

Retirement: the continuing partners gain the retiring partner's share. Gaining ratio = new share − old share. Entry: Continuing Partners' Capital A/cs Dr (gaining ratio), To Retiring Partner's Capital A/c (his share of goodwill).
Death: the same entry, crediting the deceased partner's capital account (payable to his legal representatives), with goodwill valued on the date of death.
In every case goodwill is not shown in the balance sheet after the adjustment.
concepts.analogy: When a player leaves the team, the players who take over his positions pay him for the advantage they gain.
concepts.work: Retirement settlements often hinge on the goodwill figure; the retiring partner's CA checks the profit adjustments before he signs.

jobs.title: Preparing the goodwill note for a new partner's admission
jobs.role: Senior article assistant in a CA firm's advisory team
jobs.situation: A design studio with two partners is admitting a third for a 20% share. The partners want goodwill "at 3 years' purchase of last year's profit" — last year included a one-time ₹6 lakh consultancy fee from a client that has since closed.
steps: Collect five years' profits and identify non-recurring items.
Recommend excluding the one-time fee and deducting a fair salary for the working partners so that profits are "maintainable".
Show the effect of simple vs weighted average and of the super-profit method in a comparison table for negotiation.
Once agreed, draft the entries: premium in cash to the old partners in their sacrificing ratio; no Goodwill Account raised.
jobs.takeaway: The valuation method matters less than the quality of the profits it is applied to.
jobs.think: The old partners want to raise Goodwill A/c at the agreed value so that their capital balances look bigger to the bank. Is that acceptable?
jobs.answer: No. Inherent goodwill cannot be recognised (AS 26); it must be adjusted through capital accounts. Raising it would overstate assets.

jobs.title: Settling a retiring partner's goodwill
jobs.situation: One of four partners retires. The deed says goodwill is two years' purchase of average profits of three years. The continuing partners will share in a new ratio that is not their old ratio.
steps: Compute the gaining ratio from the new and old shares — not the old ratio.
Value goodwill per the deed after adjusting abnormal items.
Debit continuing partners in the gaining ratio and credit the retiring partner; write off any goodwill already in the books in the old ratio (all four partners).
Carry the retiring partner's balance to his loan account if payment is deferred.
jobs.takeaway: Retirement uses the gaining ratio; using the old ratio is the classic error.
jobs.think: If one continuing partner's share actually falls after the retirement, how is he treated?
jobs.answer: He has a sacrifice, not a gain, so he is credited (compensated) along with the retiring partner, and the gainers bear the total.

options: Is not recognised as an asset
Is recognised at a valuer's estimate
Is recognised only on admission of a partner
Is recognised and amortised over 10 years
mcqs.explain: It is not identifiable and its cost cannot be measured reliably, so it is never recognised; only purchased goodwill may be recorded.

mcqs.q: Profits of the last three years are ₹90,000, ₹1,20,000 and ₹1,50,000 (weights 1, 2, 3). The weighted average profit is:
Average profit ₹1,80,000; capital employed ₹10,00,000; normal rate 12%. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit is:
mcqs.explain: Super profit = 1,80,000 − 1,20,000 = 60,000; × 3 = ₹1,80,000. ₹5,40,000 wrongly uses average profit; ₹5,00,000 is capitalisation of super profit.

mcqs.q: Average profit ₹90,000; normal rate of return 12%; net assets ₹6,20,000. Goodwill by capitalisation of average profit is:
X and Y share 3:2. Z is admitted and the new ratio is 2:2:1. The sacrificing ratio of X and Y is:
options: 1:0 (only X sacrifices)
mcqs.explain: X: 3/5 − 2/5 = 1/5; Y: 2/5 − 2/5 = 0. Only X sacrifices, so all of Z's goodwill goes to X.

mcqs.q: A and B share 5:3. C joins for 1/4 share (nothing said about who gives it up) and brings ₹40,000 as premium for goodwill. A's share of the premium is:
mcqs.explain: When only the newcomer's share is given, old partners sacrifice in the old ratio 5:3 → A gets 5/8 × 40,000 = ₹25,000.

mcqs.q: The incoming partner pays the premium for goodwill privately to the old partners. In the firm's books:
options: No entry is passed for goodwill
Goodwill A/c is debited
Premium A/c is credited
Old partners' capital accounts are credited
mcqs.explain: The money never passes through the firm, so nothing is recorded for it.

mcqs.q: Goodwill already appearing in the books at the time of admission is:
options: Written off among old partners in the old ratio
Written off among all partners in the new ratio
Left in the balance sheet
Credited to the new partner
mcqs.explain: It belongs to the old set-up, so the old partners write it off in their old ratio.

mcqs.q: A, B and C share 3:2:1. C retires; A and B will share equally. The gaining ratio of A and B is:
options: 0:1 — only B gains
mcqs.explain: A: 1/2 − 1/2 = 0; B: 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. Only B gains, so B alone compensates C.

mcqs.q: Super profit ₹25,000 is expected for 5 years; the present value of an annuity of ₹1 for 5 years at 12% is 3.6048. Goodwill by the annuity method is:
Which of the following does NOT affect the value of a firm's goodwill?
options: The depreciation method used in its books
Location of the business
Managerial skill
Possession of trademarks and patents
mcqs.explain: Goodwill depends on the ability to earn super profits; a bookkeeping choice of depreciation method does not create that ability.

mcqs.q: The weighted average method is preferred when past profits:
options: Show a clear rising or falling trend
Fluctuate with no pattern
Are all equal
Include losses in some years
mcqs.explain: Weights give more importance to recent years, which suits a trend.

mcqs.q: A, B and C share equally and change to 3:2:1. Goodwill is ₹1,20,000. The adjusting entry is:
options: A's Capital Dr ₹20,000; To C's Capital ₹20,000
C's Capital Dr ₹20,000; To A's Capital ₹20,000
A's Capital Dr ₹20,000; To B's and C's Capital ₹10,000 each
No entry is needed
mcqs.explain: A gains 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6 (₹20,000); B no change; C sacrifices 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6 (₹20,000). Gainer debited, sacrificer credited.

questions.q: Explain the accounting treatment of goodwill on reconstitution of a partnership firm in the light of the accounting standard on intangible assets.

items: AS 26 allows an intangible asset to be recognised only if it is identifiable, its future benefits are controlled and probable, and its cost can be measured reliably.
Inherent (self-generated) goodwill meets none of these conditions — no price has been paid for it — so it cannot be recorded. Only purchased goodwill can appear in the books.

On admission, retirement, death or change in ratio, Goodwill Account is not raised. The agreed value is adjusted through partners' capital accounts: gaining/new partners debited, sacrificing/outgoing partners credited (or premium brought in cash credited to sacrificers).
Any goodwill already in the books is written off immediately among the old partners in their old ratio.

scheme.pt: Inherent goodwill not recognised; only purchased goodwill
Adjustment through capital accounts (gainers Dr, sacrificers Cr)
Existing goodwill written off in old ratio

remarks: Answers that only listed valuation methods missed the point of the question.
Naming the standard and stating the recognition conditions earned the first mark easily.
mistakes: Saying goodwill is raised and then written off in the new ratio (an outdated method).
Confusing sacrificing ratio with gaining ratio for retirement.
tips: Four crisp points, one per mark.

remarks: Dividing weighted profits by 3 instead of the sum of weights (6) was the most common slip.
mistakes: Dividing by the number of years in a weighted average.
Using the old ratio 2:2 as the gaining ratio without checking.
tips: Show the weight table — it earns marks even if the arithmetic slips.

summary: Goodwill = value of reputation that yields profits above normal; an intangible asset.
AS 26: inherent goodwill is never recognised; only purchased goodwill. On reconstitution adjust through capital accounts; write off existing goodwill in the old ratio.
Average profit method: adjusted average (simple or weighted) × years' purchase.
Super profit = average profit − capital employed × NRR; goodwill = super profit × years, × annuity factor, or ÷ NRR.
Admission → sacrificing ratio; retirement/death → gaining ratio; change in ratio → gainers pay sacrificers.
remember: Sacrifice = old − new; gain = new − old.
Only newcomer's share given → sacrifice in old ratio.
Capitalisation of super profit = capitalisation of average profit − capital employed.
traps: Don't raise Goodwill A/c on reconstitution.
Don't divide a weighted total by the number of years.
Don't include goodwill or non-trade investments in capital employed.
Don't assume the gaining ratio equals the new ratio.

viva.q: What is goodwill, and which factors affect its value?
viva.model: Goodwill is the value of the reputation of a firm that enables it to earn profits above the normal profits of similar firms in future. It is an intangible asset. Its value depends on factors like the quality of goods, the location, the personal reputation and managerial skill of the owners, monopoly rights, and trademarks and patents.

viva.q: Why is goodwill not raised in the books on admission or retirement of a partner?
viva.model: Because of AS 26 on intangible assets. Goodwill that the firm has built itself is internally generated or inherent goodwill. It is not identifiable and its cost cannot be measured reliably since nothing was paid for it, so it cannot be recognised. Only purchased goodwill can be recorded. So on reconstitution the value of goodwill is adjusted through the partners' capital accounts instead.

viva.q: Explain the super profit method of valuing goodwill.
viva.model: First find normal profit by applying the normal rate of return to the capital employed. Super profit is the average maintainable profit minus the normal profit. Goodwill is then the super profit multiplied by the agreed number of years' purchase. Alternatively it can be valued by the annuity method, discounting the super profits, or by capitalising the super profit at the normal rate of return.

Super profit = average profit − normal profit

viva.q: How is goodwill treated when a new partner is admitted?
viva.model: If the new partner brings his share of goodwill in cash as premium, Bank is debited and the old partners' capital accounts are credited in their sacrificing ratio. If he cannot bring it in cash, his capital account is debited and the old partners' capital accounts are credited in the sacrificing ratio. If he pays the premium privately to the old partners, no entry is made in the firm's books. Existing goodwill is written off in the old ratio.

viva.q: Which ratio is used to adjust goodwill on retirement or death, and how is it calculated?
viva.model: On retirement or death the gaining ratio is used, because the continuing partners gain the share of the outgoing partner. Gaining ratio is the new share minus the old share of each continuing partner. The continuing partners' capital accounts are debited in the gaining ratio and the retiring partner's or deceased partner's capital account is credited with his share of goodwill.

viva.q: When would you use a weighted average instead of a simple average of profits?
viva.model: A weighted average is used when past profits show a clear rising or falling trend, so that recent years, which better reflect the future, get more weight; the highest weight goes to the latest year. When profits fluctuate without any clear trend, a simple average is used.

cases.title: Sohan & Mohan admit Rohan
cases.case: Sohan and Mohan share profits 3:1. On 1 April 2026 they admit Rohan for a 1/5 share, which he takes entirely from Sohan. Goodwill will be taken as twice (2 years' purchase) the average profit of the last three years: ₹1,40,000, ₹1,60,000 and ₹1,80,000. Rohan brings ₹2,50,000 as capital but only ₹40,000 towards his share of goodwill in cash. No goodwill appears in the books.

mcqs.q: The new profit-sharing ratio of Sohan, Mohan and Rohan is:
Goodwill of the firm is valued at:
Total amount credited to Sohan's capital for goodwill (cash plus adjustment) is:
mcqs.explain: Rohan's share 3,20,000 × 1/5 = ₹64,000; Sohan is the only sacrificer, so he gets all of it. ₹48,000 wrongly splits 3:1.

mcqs.q: The entry for the goodwill not brought in cash is:
options: Rohan's Capital A/c Dr ₹24,000; To Sohan's Capital A/c
Goodwill A/c Dr ₹24,000; To Sohan's Capital A/c
Sohan's Capital A/c Dr ₹24,000; To Rohan's Capital A/c
No entry is required
mcqs.explain: The shortfall of ₹24,000 is charged to Rohan's capital and credited to the sacrificing partner; Goodwill A/c is never raised.
